# Psalm 84 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 84:6 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** Blessed the-man whose-strength is-in-you, highways in-their-heart.
- **LOGOS:** Blessed are those whose strength is in you, in whose heart are the highways to Zion.
- **PNEUMA:** How happy are those who find their strength in you, whose hearts are set on making the pilgrimage.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 84:10 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** Our-shield see O-God, and-look-upon the-face-of your-anointed.
- **LOGOS:** Behold our shield, O God; look on the face of your anointed!
- **PNEUMA:** God, look with favor on our king — look at the face of your anointed one!

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 84:13 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** O-YHWH of-hosts, blessed the-man trusting in-you.
- **LOGOS:** O LORD of hosts, blessed is the one who trusts in you!
- **PNEUMA:** LORD of Angel Armies — how happy is the person who trusts in you!

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 84:4 (overlap: 3%)

- **EMET:** Also a-bird has-found a-home, and-a-swallow a-nest for-herself where she-has-placed her-young — your-altars, O-YHWH of-hosts, my-King and-my-God.
- **LOGOS:** Even the sparrow finds a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young, at your altars, O LORD of hosts, my King and my God.
- **PNEUMA:** Even the sparrow has found a home near your altar, and the swallow has built a nest where she can raise her babies — right there at your altars, LORD of Angel Armies, my King and my God.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 84:11 (overlap: 4%)

- **EMET:** For better a-day in-your-courts than-a-thousand; I-choose to-stand-at-the-threshold in-house-of my-God than-to-dwell in-tents-of wickedness.
- **LOGOS:** For a day in your courts is better than a thousand elsewhere. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than dwell in the tents of wickedness.
- **PNEUMA:** One day spent in your courtyards is better than a thousand anywhere else. I'd rather stand at the door of God's house than live comfortably in the homes of the wicked.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 84:5 (overlap: 7%)

- **EMET:** Blessed are-those dwelling in-your-house; still they-will-praise-you. Selah.
- **LOGOS:** Blessed are those who dwell in your house, ever singing your praise! Selah
- **PNEUMA:** How happy are those who live in your house — they never stop praising you! Selah

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.
